issues.display_title: Issue #188: perf: grid lag + 100% disk usage on folders with tens of thousands of images
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.15.19.47.mov

What happens

Opening a folder with tens of thousands of images makes the browse grid stutter while scrolling, and disk usage stays at 100% for minutes after scrolling stops.

Cause: every ImageItem fires get-thumb the moment its card mounts. Fast scrolling mounts and unmounts thousands of cards; the renderer cancels its own promise on unmount but the backend does not, so each stale request still queues a full-file decode behind thumb_semaphore. Scrolling past 10k images enqueues ~10k decodes for thumbnails nobody is looking at any more — the disk reads whole source files (a 32MP panorama in full, per decode), and the thumbnails actually on screen wait behind that backlog. get_thumb made it worse by acquiring a semaphore permit before checking the cache, so even a cache hit queued.

Second, independent load: the GPS sweep (extract_gps_data) reads EXIF for every image in the folder via par_iter. Chunked and cancellable, but unbounded — a 30k-panorama folder is minutes of sustained I/O right after the folder opens, competing with thumbnail decodes.

How to reproduce

  1. Open a folder with 10k+ images (Preview or File Manager).
  2. Scroll fast to the bottom and back.
  3. Scroll stutters; disk usage stays at 100% long after scrolling stops.

Goal

Scrolling a 10k+ image folder stays smooth, and disk I/O settles shortly after the user stops scrolling — no work left running for thumbnails already scrolled past.

  • src/renderer/features/preview/ImageItem.tsx — request the thumbnail only after the card stays mounted ~150ms, so cards that fly past never hit IPC. Shared component: covers Preview / Edit / File Manager grids.
  • src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs (get_thumb) — check the thumbnail cache (one stat) before acquiring a semaphore permit, so a cache hit returns immediately instead of queueing behind in-flight decodes.
  • src-tauri/src/commands/metadata.rs (extract_gps_data) — throttled instead of capped: coordinates are only known after the EXIF read, so a viewport-driven sweep is impossible for uncached files, and a hard cap would leave a big folder's map showing partial markers with no signal which are missing. The sweep now waits 1.5s before its first read (thumbnails on screen get the disk first, and leaving during the delay costs nothing) and reads on a dedicated 4-thread rayon pool instead of the global one, so it no longer takes every core off the thumbnail decodes. Markers stay complete.
  • src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs (get_thumb) — a queued request captures PREWARM_GENERATION (bumped on every folder load) before waiting for its semaphore permit and drops itself if the generation moved while it waited, so navigating away no longer leaves the previous folder's decodes running. Returns "" for a dropped request; ImageItem retries once after 400ms so a same-folder reload (card still mounted, effect never re-runs) can't leave a permanent placeholder. Scroll-past inside one folder is still handled by the 150ms settle delay — the two cover different cases.

Done on branch fix/loadfolder; pnpm typecheck + cargo check clean (the 2 cargo clippy errors in nadir.rs / pano_level are pre-existing and untouched).

🧪 QA Tester Summary — Issue #188: perf: grid lag + 100% disk usage on folders with tens of thousands of images

QA Date: September 14, 2026
Target Application: GoThru Photo Studio Desktop (Tauri v2 + Rust) v1.1.10
Test Environment: Windows 11 Real Device
Test Data: Large fixture directory of 10,000 images (C:\Users\Work\qa-issue188-test\large_folder_10k) & secondary folder (folder_a)
Verdict: PASSED (100% Acceptance & Parity)

1. Executive Summary

End-to-end performance verification on a Windows 11 real desktop application with a 10,000-image dataset confirms that Issue #188 is completely resolved:

  1. Debounced Thumbnail Requests (~150ms settle): Rapid scrolling past thousands of image cards in both File Manager grid and Preview bottom browse strip no longer triggers stale thumbnail IPC calls. Cards that fly past during scroll never hit the backend decoding queue.
  2. Instant Cache Check Before Semaphore: get_thumb checks the thumbnail cache (stat) before acquiring the thumb_semaphore permit, ensuring cached items return instantaneously without queuing behind in-flight decodes.
  3. Stale Decode Dropping via PREWARM_GENERATION: Navigating away from a folder immediately drops pending decodes waiting for semaphore permits in the backend, returning empty string and freeing disk I/O immediately.
  4. GPS Sweep Throttling & Dedicated Pool: extract_gps_data starts with a 1.5s delay and runs on a dedicated 4-thread rayon pool, eliminating disk seek storms and core starvation during initial folder load.

All 4 core test scenarios (TC-01 through TC-04) passed with a 100% success rate.

2. Code Review & Architecture Analysis

File / Module Component Key Implementation & Review Findings Quality Gate
src/renderer/features/preview/ImageItem.tsx ImageItem (L17–L70) • 150ms Settle Debounce: Defers ipc.getThumbnail call by 150ms; cancels timer on unmount.
• Retry on Generation Drop: Retries once after 400ms if backend drops a queued request on folder reload.		 ✅ Passed
src-tauri/src/commands/image.rs get_thumb (L398–L426) • Early Cache Hit: Stat-checks existing cache file before acquiring semaphore permit.
• Generation Guard: Captures PREWARM_GENERATION and aborts if folder changed while waiting for permit.		 ✅ Passed
src-tauri/src/commands/metadata.rs extract_gps_data (L142–L190) • 1.5s Initial Delay: Waits 1500ms before reading EXIF to let viewport thumbnails take disk priority.
• Dedicated Rayon Pool: Runs on dedicated 4-thread pool instead of global pool.		 ✅ Passed

3. Verification & Test Case Results

TC-02 Fast Scroll & Settle Debounce Rapidly scroll mouse wheel down 5000+ items and stop No disk 100% lockup; thumbnails render cleanly upon settle Scrolling was fluid; thumbnails loaded within 150ms of stopping ✅ PASSED
TC-03 Preview Browse Strip Performance Switch to Preview and rapidly scroll bottom strip Smooth horizontal scrolling without UI hitching Strip scrolled smoothly and settled cleanly ✅ PASSED
TC-04 Cancel Stale Decodes on Navigation Navigate away to another folder while large folder is active Backend drops queued requests; new folder loads instantly New folder loaded in <1s; zero lingering disk thrashing ✅ PASSED

issues.display_title: Issue #195: Image Info panel: minimize by dragging instead of hiding
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.14.49.46.mov

The Image Info (metadata) panel in the preview can be resized, but the 5px separator is invisible as an affordance and the panel cannot be swiped away: it stops at minSize and the only way to close it is the header X / the View-menu toggle, which unmounts it entirely so there is no way to bring it back by gesture.

Scope

  • Add a visible grip handle centered on the metadata separator so the drag target is discoverable.
  • Make the panel collapsible: dragging the grip down past the minimum collapses it to 0 instead of stopping.
  • Keep the separator + grip visible while collapsed, so it can be dragged back up. Never disappear entirely.
  • Header X becomes a minimize (chevron-down) that collapses the panel instead of hiding it.
  • E shortcut / View → Image Info toggles collapsed vs expanded, using the same state, so the menu check mark stays in sync.
  • Fix separator cursor: horizontal separators used col-resize; should be row-resize.
  • Do not persist a collapsed (0px) size to the stored layout — re-opening must restore a usable height.

Files

  • src/renderer/features/preview/Main.tsx — grip, collapsible panel, expand/collapse effect, resize→redux sync, layout-save guard
  • src/renderer/features/preview/Metadata.tsx — minimize button
  • src/renderer/index.css — row-resize cursor

Verification

pnpm typecheck clean; manual check of all three close paths (drag, minimize button, E) plus restoring by dragging the grip back up.

🧪 QA Tester Summary — Issue #195: Image Info panel: minimize by dragging instead of hiding

QA Date: September 14, 2026
Target Application: GoThru Photo Studio Desktop (Tauri v2 + Rust) v1.1.10
Test Environment: Windows 11 Real Device (Installed Packaged App)
Test Data: Authentic 360 Panoramas in C:\Users\Work\qa-issue187-test\folder_a
Verdict: PASSED (100% Acceptance & Parity)

1. Executive Summary

End-to-end verification on a Windows 11 real device confirms that Issue #195 is fully resolved:

  1. Visible Grip Handle Affordance: A pill grip handle is centered on the metadata separator (.group/metagrip), making the drag target easily discoverable.
  2. Collapsible Panel on Drag Down: Dragging the grip handle down past the minimum threshold smoothly collapses the panel to height 0 rather than locking up.
  3. Persistent Separator & Grip in Collapsed State: When collapsed to 0, the separator and grip handle remain visible at the bottom of the viewer, allowing the user to pull/drag it back up anytime.
  4. Header Minimize Button (chevron-down): The previous header close icon (X) is replaced with a minimize chevron-down button that collapses the panel cleanly without unmounting it.
  5. Shortcut E & Menu Sync: Pressing keyboard shortcut E and toggling View -> Image Info drives isShowMetaData expanded vs collapsed state, keeping menu checkmarks perfectly in sync.
  6. Correct Cursor Style: Horizontal separators correctly use row-resize cursor.
  7. Stored Layout Guard: Collapsed sizes (0px) are ignored from the persisted layout so reopening or restarting always restores a usable default height.

All 5 core test scenarios (TC-01 through TC-05) passed with a 100% success rate.

2. Code Review & Architecture Analysis

File / Module Component / Target Key Implementation & Review Findings Quality Gate
src/renderer/features/preview/Main.tsx Main (L380–L408) • Grip Pill: Added centered visual grab pill with hover states inside Separator.
• Collapsible Panel: Configured collapsible, collapsedSize={0}, minSize={60}.
• State Latch: Drives defaultSize={layout.isShowMetaData ? 100 : 0} without unmounting the separator.		 ✅ Passed
src/renderer/features/preview/Metadata.tsx Metadata (L50–L60) • Chevron-down Minimize: Header button uses fa-chevron-down with onMinimize trigger. ✅ Passed
src/renderer/index.css CSS rules • Horizontal separators use row-resize cursor. ✅ Passed

3. Verification & Test Case Results

TC-03 Shortcut 'E' Toggle Press keyboard shortcut E Metadata panel expands back to usable height Panel re-expanded immediately ✅ PASSED
TC-04 Drag Down to Collapse Drag grip handle downward with mouse Panel collapses to 0 height smoothly past threshold Panel collapsed to 0; separator retained ✅ PASSED

issues.display_title: Issue #57: Watermark Output With Dense GoThru Logo For Non-Subscribers
issues.main_description_html:
Source

User feedback:

Goal

Instead of blocking non-subscribed users from features, open the features to everyone but watermark the output with a dense GoThru logo for non-subscribers (PtGui-style).

Scope

  • Apply a dense/tiled GoThru logo watermark to output (stitching output first; confirm whether it applies to other feature outputs too).
  • Gate watermark on subscription state: non-subscribers get watermarked output; paid/Pro users get clean, watermark-free output.
  • Match the PtGui approach (dense tiled overlay, not a single corner mark).

Open questions

  • Which outputs/features does the watermark apply to (stitching only, or all Pro features)?
  • Watermark density/opacity/branding spec.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Non-subscribed users can use the feature(s), but output is watermarked with a dense GoThru logo.
  2. Paid/Pro users receive clean, un-watermarked output.
  3. Watermark visibility is driven by subscription state.

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

🧪 QA Tester Summary — Issue #57: Watermark Output With Dense GoThru Logo For Non-Subscribers

QA Date: September 14, 2026
Target Application: GoThru Photo Studio Desktop (Tauri v2 + Rust) v1.1.10
Test Account: minime@grr.la (Non-Subscriber / Free Account)
Test Environment: Windows 11 Real Device (Installed App)
Verdict: PASSED (100% Acceptance & Parity)

1. Executive Summary

End-to-end verification on a Windows 11 real desktop application using a non-subscribed / free user account (minime@grr.la) confirms that Issue #57 is completely resolved:

  1. Unblocked Feature Access for Free Users: Non-subscribed / free users are no longer blocked by subscription restriction modals when opening Stitch 360 / Edit features.
  2. Dense Watermark Policy: Output panoramas generated by non-paying users automatically receive a dense, tiled semi-transparent GoThru watermark (assets/images/stitching/watermark-tile.png) composited across the panorama.
  3. Clean Output for Paid Subscribers: Users with active Pro subscriptions (hasPaidAccessFromUserDetail) receive clean, un-watermarked outputs without any logo overlay.
  4. Fail-Closed Compositing: If watermark application fails during processing, the task reports Failed to prevent accidental release of un-watermarked images to non-subscribers.

All 3 core acceptance criteria have been verified with 100% compliance.

2. Code Review & Architecture Analysis

File / Module Component Key Implementation & Review Findings Quality Gate
src/renderer/components/features/Edit/Stitching/hooks/useStitching.ts useStitching (L435–L445) • Computes watermark: !hasPaidAccessFromUserDetail(userDetail) and passes it in stitching configuration payload. ✅ Passed
src-tauri/src/commands/stitching.rs apply_watermark & run_one (L750–L960) • Scales watermark tile grid based on output image resolution (watermark_cell_size).
• Composites WATERMARK_TILE in-place using image crate.
• Fail-closed error handling.		 ✅ Passed

issues.display_title: Issue #58: Make Stitching Free/ Live While in Beta
issues.main_description_html:
Source

User feedback:

Goal

Make the Stitching feature free and available (live) to all users while it is in Beta.

Scope

  • Ship Stitching as a Beta feature, free for everyone during the beta period.
  • Label/indicate Beta status in the UI.
  • Ensure no paywall/Pro gate blocks Stitching during Beta (coordinate with the watermark-for-non-subscribers approach — separate issue).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Stitching is accessible to all users (free) while flagged Beta.
  2. Beta status is clearly communicated in the UI.
  3. Gating can later be re-enabled when Stitching exits Beta.

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-07-09.at.13.51.03.mov

  4. Interactive Workflow Ready: Settings (projections, blending modes, output directories, advanced tuning) and queue board are fully functional and ready for stitching operations.

All 3 core acceptance criteria have been verified with 100% compliance.
